v: After these things, Jesus was walking in Galilee, for he wouldn’t walk in Judea, because the Jews sought to kill him.
Now the feast of the Jews, the Feast of Booths, was at hand.
His brothers therefore said to him, “Depart from here and go into Judea, that your disciples also may see your works which you do.
For no one does anything in secret while he seeks to be known openly. If you do these things, reveal yourself to the world.”
For even his brothers didn’t believe in him.
b: When we enter John chapter 7, the atmosphere clearly shifts. From the teaching about “the bread of life” in chapter 6 to the “division in how people respond to Jesus” here, the stronger the light shines, the more the reactions of the heart are revealed. This passage shows us three attitudes toward Jesus: the hostility of enemies, the unbelief of family, and the eyes of the world.
The passage begins:
“After these things, Jesus was walking in Galilee, for he wouldn't walk in Judea, because the Jews sought to kill him.”

Jesus was not running away; He was working according to the Heavenly Father's timing. He was not frightened off by threats, and not shaken by human attacks. He followed only the Father's will and did not act on His own timetable.

His life was completely surrendered under the Father's will, with no self, no pride, no impatience, no insisting on His own ideas. He knew that when “the time had not yet come” He would not act, and when “the time had come” He would not hesitate.
This is true obedience, and the deepest power of spiritual life.
Then verse 2 says:
“Now the Jewish feast of Booths was at hand.”

The Feast of Booths was one of the three great feasts of the Jewish year, representing joy, thanksgiving, and the presence of God. Yet at that moment Judea was full of murderous intent, plotting, and unbelief. The feast symbolized God's presence, but the people's hearts rejected the One whom God had sent.
A person can keep the feast and yet not know God; can worship in ritual and yet not worship Jesus.
Verses 3 and 4 bring out a heartbreaking scene:

“His brothers therefore said to him, ‘Depart from here, and go into Judea, that your disciples also may see your works which you do. For no one does anything in secret, and himself seeks to be known openly. If you do these things, reveal yourself to the world.’”
This sounds like concern, but it is actually mockery, and also a kind of testing.

What they mean is much like: “If you are really that great, go to the big city and show yourself; if you are going to do miracles, prove it to everyone in public; don't waste your talent out in the countryside.”
The advice they gave did not come from faith or from reverence but from the world's way of seeing:
To succeed, you must be exposed; to have status, you must be seen; to become famous, you must seize the opportunity.
They did not understand at all that Jesus' way is not performance, not competition, not proving Himself, but humbling Himself, obeying, giving Himself up, and walking the way of the cross.
Verse 5 gives the real reason:
“For even his brothers didn't believe in him.”
What hurts most is not the opposition of enemies but the unbelief of those closest to us. The deepest misunderstanding is not from strangers but from your own household.
Jesus experienced all of this. His brothers did not see that He was the Son of God, did not see His mission, and did not see His identity.

Unbelief makes people look at Jesus with the wrong eyes: seeing Him as a performer, a competitor, a religious figure, a political hope, a special person among the relatives, yet not seeing that He is the Son of the living God.
This passage reminds us:
First, Jesus never acts on impulse or because of circumstances, but entirely according to the Father's timing. True spiritual power is surrender, not drive.
Second, the outward bustle of a feast does not mean people truly know God. Religion can flourish while hearts are far from God.
Third, even those closest to Jesus may still not believe. Unbelief is not a matter of distance but of the heart.
Fourth, unbelief makes people measure Jesus by the world's methods. People will advise Him to “show yourself,” but Jesus walks the way of “giving Himself up.”
Fifth, even when misunderstood, persecuted, and challenged, Jesus stood firm in the Father's will. He was not shaken by people's opinions and did not stop moving forward because of their unbelief.
q: Have you ever drifted from God's timing and direction because of people's opinions, expectations, or pressure?
Today, are you willing to learn from Jesus, to place everything in the Father's hands and act only according to His will?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, make our hearts like Jesus, not acting according to our own will but seeking Your will. Help us no longer look at You with the world's eyes but know who You are by faith. Keep our hearts, so that when we are not understood or are misunderstood, we still walk only in Your timing and Your will. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: Jesus therefore said to them, “My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready.
The world can’t hate you, but it hates me, because I testify about it, that its works are evil.
You go up to the feast. I am not yet going up to this feast, because my time is not yet fulfilled.”
Having said these things to them, he stayed in Galilee.
b: This passage continues Jesus' response to His brothers, but in it the Lord reveals the core principle of His life—everything He does is according to the Father's timing alone, not human suggestions, the push of circumstances, emotional reactions, or the ways of the world.
Jesus first says to His brothers:
“My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready.”
This sentence uncovers two completely different ways of living:
One, the life of Jesus:
According to the Father's time.
Two, the life of His brothers:
According to their own convenience.
The difference between these two lives is the difference between heavenly and worldly.

“My time”—not man's time, not the time of circumstances, but the time set by the Heavenly Father. Jesus was not rushed by people, not driven by pressure, not hurried by circumstances, not reactive to challenges. He did not do “what looked like it should be done”; He did only “what the Father wanted done.”
His life had only one rhythm—the Father's rhythm.
On the contrary: “Your time is always ready.” It means:

You do whatever you want; you go whenever you want; you show yourselves whenever you want; your judgments are based on “convenience,” “opportunity,” “benefit,” “reputation,” “performance.” You do not wait on God and do not seek God's timing.
This is exactly the way of the world: catch the moment, seize the opportunity, find a stage, seek exposure, demand success.
But Jesus was not like this. He was centered on the Heavenly Father, not on Himself. He was emptied of self, humble, and completely surrendered.
Then Jesus says another powerful sentence:
“The world can't hate you, but it hates me, because I testify about it, that its works are evil.”

Why could the world not hate His brothers? Because they were of the same nature as the world. The world does not hate those who are like it; the world hates only those who let it see its own darkness.

Jesus was hated not because He made mistakes, not because He confronted people, but because His holiness showed up the world's sin, His truth showed up people's problems, His light showed up people's darkness.
Light does not flatter darkness, truth does not compliment sin, life does not cater to death.
Jesus did not come to please people; He came to save people. And the first step of saving is to reveal the truth about sin.
He does not condemn people; He points out sin so that people may be saved.

So darkness hates light, sin hates truth, and self hates surrender. This is also the difference between Jesus and His brothers: they did not live out the truth, so the world did not hate them; but Jesus lived out the truth, so the world hated Him.
This is the path every true disciple will necessarily walk.
Finally, Jesus says to His brothers:
“You go up to the feast. I am not yet going up to this feast, because my time is not yet fulfilled.”

He was not refusing to go; He was “not going now.” He was not rejecting the feast but refusing to move according to man's timetable. He knew the Father's time had not yet come, so He remained at rest, quiet, and waiting.
The passage ends with a narrative line:
“Having said these things to them, he stayed in Galilee.”
Staying in Galilee—it looked as though nothing was being done, nothing changed, no action, no exposure. But that was the moment when He was “most in the Father's will.”
For Jesus, obedience is the deepest action, waiting is the strongest power, and rest is the most important service.
This passage reminds us:
First, spiritual life is not about looking active but about whether we follow God's timing. When His time has not come, we do not move. When His time comes, we do not hesitate.
Second, the world values “convenience,” but Jesus values “obedience.” The world talks efficiency; Jesus talks God's will.
Third, the world did not hate His brothers because they were of the same nature as the world; but Jesus was hated because of the truth. If we live out His life, we will meet the same treatment.

Fourth, true spiritual power is the ability to move when it is time to move and to wait when it is time to wait. This is called surrender, self-denial, and obedience to the leading of the Holy Spirit.
q: Are your actions right now according to your own “convenience” or according to the Lord's “time”?
Are you willing to learn from Jesus, to rest, wait, and surrender before the Father's time has come?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, help us no longer live according to our own convenience or emotions, but learn like Jesus to move only according to Your timing. Help us not to fear waiting, not to fear silence, not to fear being unknown, but to long to walk in Your will. And make us willing to live out the truth, remaining faithful and unchanged even when misunderstood by the world. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: But when his brothers had gone up to the feast, then he also went up, not publicly, but as it were in secret.
The Jews therefore sought him at the feast, and said, “Where is he?”
There was much murmuring among the multitudes concerning him. Some said, “He is a good man.” Others said, “Not so, but he leads the multitude astray.”
Yet no one spoke openly of him for fear of the Jews.
b: This passage uncovers a profound spiritual phenomenon: truth always stirs up talk among people, but few are willing to stand on the side of truth. Jesus' entrance into the scene of the Feast of Booths also shows us the wisdom of how He acted, His attitude in facing hostility, and the various reactions of the human heart toward Him.
The passage first records:
“But when his brothers had gone up to the feast, then he also went up, not publicly, but as it were in secret.”
Jesus did not go at once at His brothers' urging, but when the Father's time came, “He also went up.” He did not refuse to go; He simply did not go on man's timetable.
“Not publicly, but as it were in secret” was not out of fear but out of obedience to the Father's leading.
He did not seek exposure and did not need people to see Him. He did not come to perform or to prove Himself, but to accomplish the Father's will.
Every step of His was under the guidance of the Holy Spirit, not flaunting, not noisy, not high-profile—yet completely in God's rhythm.
Then verse 11 says:
“The Jews sought him at the feast, and said, ‘Where is he?’”
This “seeking” was not a longing to receive life, nor a desire to know Him, but “wanting to seize Him, catch Him in a fault, get rid of Him.”
The world sometimes seems to be seeking Jesus, but the motive may not be faith but opposition; not seeking truth but wanting to overthrow truth.
Those who truly seek the Lord do not look with their eyes but seek with their hearts.
Verse 12 describes the reaction of the crowd:
“There was much murmuring among the multitudes concerning him.”
Jesus always makes Himself impossible to ignore. His words do not let people stay neutral, His life does not let people stay indifferent, His truth does not let people stay vague.
So two extreme reactions appeared in the crowd:
One, “He is a good man.”

These people affirmed His good deeds, His healing, His compassion, His teaching. But they thought of Him only as a good teacher, a good rabbi, a good prophet—and did not see that He is the Son of God. Many people like Jesus' “example” but reject Jesus' “lordship.”
Two, “He leads the multitude astray.”

These people did not believe His identity, questioned His motives, and even thought He was undermining the system and deceiving the people. They saw the miracles but were unwilling to admit the truth; they saw His life but insisted on resisting His light.
The same Jesus divides people's hearts into two sides—and this division still exists today.
Verse 13 reveals a deeper condition of the heart:
“Yet no one spoke openly of him for fear of the Jews.”
They talked, but did not dare to take a stand; they spoke in private, but did not dare in public; they thought it in their hearts, but did not dare to admit it.
Why? Because of—fear.
Fear of losing position, fear of losing acceptance, fear of being excluded, fear of being attacked, fear of being different from the mainstream.
They did not lack truth; they lacked courage. It was not that they did not know Jesus' words were true, but that they did not dare to stand on the side of truth.
When a person is centered on “human opinion,” he cannot stand openly in “God's truth.”
This passage reminds us:
First, Jesus does not act according to human expectations but according to the Father's timing. Spiritual life is not driven by outside pressure but led by the Holy Spirit.
Second, people's reactions to Jesus are always divided—some say He is a good man, some say He leads the multitude astray. Few truly recognize Him as Lord.
Third, many like to talk about Jesus in private but do not dare to acknowledge Him publicly. The reason is not unbelief but fear.
Fourth, truth is not for discussing but for standing on. Those who do not stand on the side of truth will always live in fear.
Fifth, Jesus walked in secret not because He was afraid, but because He was emptied of self and obedient, acting only according to the Father's will.
q: Have you ever been afraid of what people think and so not dared to acknowledge Jesus openly?
Are you willing to ask the Lord for courage, so that in any setting you dare to stand openly on the side of truth?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, help us no longer follow Jesus in the world's way but learn from Him to be obedient to Your timing. Help us no longer merely talk about Jesus but stand boldly on His side, not fearing people's eyes but looking only to Your will. Make our hearts sincere toward You, firm in the truth, and unafraid of the world. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: But when it was now the middle of the feast, Jesus went up into the temple and taught.
The Jews therefore marveled, saying, “How does this man know letters, having never been educated?”
Jesus therefore answered them, “My teaching is not mine, but his who sent me.
If anyone desires to do his will, he will know about the teaching, whether it is from God, or if I am speaking from myself.
b: This passage takes us into the heart of Jesus' public teaching, and also into the heart of all spiritual learning—truth is not grasped by the mind but by the surrender of the heart; not by clever study but by the revelation that obedience brings.
The passage begins:
“But when it was now the midst of the feast, Jesus went up into the temple and taught.”

He did not act on His brothers' timetable, but when the Heavenly Father's time came, He walked into the temple—not to perform, not to prove anything, not to debate, but to fulfill the mission He was sent for: to teach the truth.
His motivation was not human expectation but the Heavenly Father's will. He stayed silent before human eyes, yet in the Father's time He was full of power.
Then verse 15 says:
“The Jews therefore marveled, saying, ‘How does this man know writing, having never been educated?’”
The Jews valued a rabbi's educational background very highly: Who did he study under? Where was he trained? What school was he from?
But Jesus did not follow their religious system. He did not take a rabbi as His teacher or enter a rabbinic school, yet His wisdom far surpassed everyone's.
So they were amazed, perplexed, even uneasy.
Their question was really: Can a person's academic credentials determine spiritual authority? Can human systems regulate God's revelation? How can someone teach us who has not learned in our way?
This shows how easily the human heart treats “knowledge” as the ticket to truth, forgetting that the source of truth is not scholarship but God Himself.
So Jesus answered:
“My teaching is not mine, but his who sent me.”
He was not shifting responsibility but declaring His identity: every word He spoke was not from Himself but from the Heavenly Father.

He did not “say whatever He wanted to say”; every word He spoke was in complete agreement with the Father. His teaching was not a human theory but God's revelation. His words were not learned but came from heaven.
He was not passing on knowledge; He was revealing God's heart.
Finally, Jesus said something extremely key, extremely upside-down, and extremely true:
“If anyone desires to do his will, he will know about the teaching, whether it is from God, or if I speak from myself.”
In this sentence Jesus uncovers the core principle of spiritual understanding:
The key to understanding truth is not the head but the heart. Not cleverness but obedience. Not understanding first and then acting, but being willing to act first, and then understanding.
The world's way is: understand → accept → act.
Jesus' way is: surrender → act → see → understand.

If a person is unwilling to surrender, even a lifetime of study will not let him truly understand truth. But a person willing to obey God's will, even if he does not understand at first, will be guided, revealed to, and made to see by God Himself.
True spiritual light does not come from research but from obedience.
This passage reminds us:
First, Jesus never acted on man's timetable but on the Father's time. In the Father's timing, He speaks naturally, teaches naturally, and fulfills His mission naturally.
Second, spiritual authority does not come from human education but from God's calling. Jesus had not been trained in the religious system, yet He possessed wisdom from heaven.
Third, if people judge only with the mind, they easily become proud like the Jews, measuring God by human ways.
Fourth, true revelation comes from obedience. “If anyone desires to do God's will, he will know about the teaching, whether it is from God.”
Fifth, faith is not understanding first and then doing, but being willing first to surrender and to believe, and then God makes us understand.
q: In seeking truth now, do you depend on understanding or on obedience?
Are you willing to say to the Lord, “I am willing to do Your will; please help me understand Your word”?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, give us a teachable heart, so that we no longer measure Your truth by human methods. Make us willing to obey first and understand afterward; to believe first and see afterward. Lead us into Your light, so that we truly know that the teaching of Jesus comes from You and is life, the way, and the truth. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: He who speaks from himself seeks his own glory, but he who seeks the glory of him who sent him is true, and no unrighteousness is in him.
Didn’t Moses give you the law, and yet none of you keeps the law? Why do you seek to kill me?”
The multitude answered, “You have a demon! Who seeks to kill you?”
b: This passage is Jesus' response to the Jews' questioning of His teaching. He brings out two things: (1) the motive behind speaking; (2) the gap between religious appearance and real life. His answer does not only respond to the question; it also shines light into the heart.
Jesus first says:
“He who speaks from himself seeks his own glory.”
He points out a spiritual principle: the source of a person's speech determines the nature of his speech.
If a person speaks from himself—in order to be seen, affirmed, respected, exalted—then however spiritual his words, they will carry unrighteousness.
A person may not look proud on the outside, but as long as the heart is seeking its own glory, the words that come out will deviate from the truth.
Then He adds the contrast:
“But he who seeks the glory of him who sent him is true, and no unrighteousness is in him.”
It means: a true servant does not want people to notice himself but to notice God. Not to highlight himself but to let the glory go to the Heavenly Father who sent him.
Jesus never sought His own glory in His whole life. All His words, all His decisions, all His actions had only one motive: that the Heavenly Father be glorified.
This is why He is true, upright, and pure. There is not a trace of unrighteousness in Him, because there is not a trace of self.
He is saying: if a person seeks God's glory, his life is true; if a person seeks his own glory, his life will be twisted by unrighteousness.
Then in verse 19 He points out the deepest problem:
“Didn't Moses give you the law, and yet none of you keeps the law? Why do you seek to kill me?”
Jesus lays bare the hypocrisy of religion:
With your mouths you honor Moses, honor the law, and say you love God, but your actions violate the most basic requirement of the law: do not murder.
What He means is: the law you value most, you yourselves do not keep. Outwardly you are spiritual, but inwardly you resist the truth.
However beautiful the religious exterior, if life is not surrendered it falls into falsehood.
As soon as Jesus said this, the people's hearts were lit up, but they were unwilling to admit the truth about themselves.
So verse 20 contains an extremely ironic line:
“You have a demon! Who seeks to kill you?”
When truth shines on people, if they are unwilling to be illumined, they attack the light, deny the light, accuse the light.
When they said Jesus “has a demon,” they were really saying: “It is not that something is wrong with us; something is wrong with you!”
But as the Gospel goes on, the people's intent to kill Jesus becomes clearer and clearer, and in the end they really did nail Him to the cross.
Those unwilling to face the truth will attack the one who points it out.
This passage reminds us:
First, the motive of speaking determines the spiritual quality of speaking. If it is for ourselves, words easily deviate from truth; if it is for God, words can bring forth life.
Second, those truly of God do not seek their own glory but seek God's will. A surrendered person has no unrighteousness in his heart.
Third, a religious exterior without life easily leads to self-deception. The Jews honored the law yet broke the law; we too may honor God's word without truly doing it.
Fourth, when truth shines into the heart, people respond in one of two ways: (1) humble surrender; (2) counterattack and denial. The more unwilling a person is to surrender, the greater his attack.
Fifth, the power of Jesus' life is that He was completely emptied of self—He did not speak His own words, did not seek His own glory, did not do His own will.
q: Are your motives in speaking and serving truly for God, or for yourself?
Today, are you willing to ask the Lord to make you a person in whom “no unrighteousness is found”?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, make our hearts pure, so that everything we say and do is for Your glory and not our own. Shine on us, so that we do not fall into the trap of religious appearance but truly do Your will. When truth shines on us, give us humility, so that we do not counterattack or hide but surrender in You. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: Jesus answered them, “I did one work and you all marvel because of it.
Moses has given you circumcision (not that it is of Moses, but of the fathers), and on the Sabbath you circumcise a boy.
If a boy receives circumcision on the Sabbath, that the law of Moses may not be broken, are you angry with me, because I made a man completely healthy on the Sabbath?
Don’t judge according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment.”
b: In this passage the theme Jesus brings out is: human eyes are often distorted, but God's eyes are always righteous. True spiritual life is to let go of judging by appearance and enter into judging by God's heart.
At the beginning, Jesus says:
“I did one work, and you all marvel because of it.”

This “one work” was the healing of the paralyzed man by the pool of Bethesda on the Sabbath (John 5). Jesus had not done many perplexing things; He had done only one—healing a man who had suffered for many years.

But the religious people accused Him and opposed Him because of the “Sabbath.” They did not see God's merciful heart, only the rules they kept; they did not see the grace of healing, only outward conduct.
This reflects a common problem of religious people: they value form over life; letter over mercy; rules over God Himself. Jesus knew this well and confronted it directly.
So He continues:
“Moses has given you circumcision (not that it is of Moses, but of the fathers), and on the Sabbath you circumcise a boy.”

Jesus points out a contradiction: in order to keep circumcision, the Jews would circumcise a baby even on the Sabbath. Why? Because circumcision is the sign of the covenant with God, and they dared not delay. In other words, they themselves made “exceptions” on the Sabbath.

Yet when Jesus healed a man who had suffered for many years, they were furious. This shows that their problem was not the law but the heart. The law was meant to bring life to people, not to make them lose life. But they turned the law into a burden, an accusation, a bondage.
Then Jesus asks:
“If a boy receives circumcision on the Sabbath, that the law of Moses may not be broken, are you angry with me, because I made a man every bit whole on the Sabbath?”

What He means is: you can act on the Sabbath in order to keep circumcision; but I may not act in order to restore a person's life? What you keep is the form; what I keep is the essence of life. You value rules; I value the Father's heart.
Jesus is saying: true rest is not doing nothing but being in agreement with the Father's heart; true obedience is not clinging to the letter but living out God's love.
Finally, Jesus speaks the most important sentence of this passage:
“Don't judge according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment.”
Judging by appearance is human nature: looking at the exterior, the ritual, the habit, the culture, other people's behavior, the way we like.
But God looks at the heart, at motives, at essence, at life. He does not judge by appearance but by truth.
“Judge righteous judgment” in the original means: “by God's standard, not man's standard.” That is—turn your eyes from earthly eyes to God's eyes; not looking at the surface but at God's heart.
This passage reminds us:
First, the religious eye easily sees rules but not life. Jesus healed a person, yet they looked only at whether the Sabbath was being “violated.”
Second, people often judge by appearance rather than by God's heart. Appearance easily deceives, and easily makes people think themselves righteous.
Third, everything Jesus did was in accord with the Father's heart. He was not destroying the Sabbath; He was restoring the true meaning of the Sabbath.
Fourth, what God values is not ritual but life. He cares more about people being healed and set free than about rigid religious appearance.
Fifth, truly spiritual people do not “look at appearance” but “judge righteous judgment”—by God's eyes, by God's truth, by God's heart.
q: Have you also ever overlooked God's true heart because of appearance, form, or human habit?
Today, are you willing to ask the Lord to give you His eyes, to see the essence of things and His will?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, remove our habit of looking at appearances, so that we no longer judge things by human standards but see everything with Your eyes. Bring our hearts back to the essence of life, not stuck in dead rules but living in Your truth and love. Help us, like Jesus, to do everything in a way that reflects Your heart. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: Therefore some of them of Jerusalem said, “Isn’t this he whom they seek to kill?
Behold, he speaks openly, and they say nothing to him. Can it be that the rulers indeed know that this is truly the Christ?
However we know where this man comes from, but when the Christ comes, no one will know where he comes from.”
b: This passage shows us three reactions of the human heart: the confused, the watchful, and the rejecting. In Jesus' public teaching, each reaction reveals the heart's attitude toward truth, and also shows how people, because of their own notions, miss the moment when God Himself comes to them.
The passage first says:
“Isn't this he whom they seek to kill?”

Among the people in Jerusalem, some had already sensed the intentions of the religious leaders and had heard that Jesus was being hunted. They knew the authorities wanted to kill Jesus and understood the political and religious opposition behind it. Yet now they saw—Jesus standing in front of everyone speaking openly, and those who wanted to kill Him did nothing to stop Him.

This puzzled them greatly. One of the greatest obstacles of the human heart to faith is “confusion” and “contradiction.” On one hand they had heard the rulers wanted to kill Him; on the other they saw the rulers doing nothing. So they began to reason, doubt, and guess.
Then they said:
“Can it be that the rulers indeed know that this is truly the Christ?”

These words reveal the wavering in their hearts: the rulers had said He was a heretic and a false prophet, but now they let Him teach publicly—could it mean the rulers were beginning to believe in Him?
Their faith was not rooted in God but in the leaders' attitude; not rooted in truth but in the voice of social mainstream.
This also exposes a common phenomenon: some people are not seeking truth but watching power and the direction of the wind.
If the rulers believe, they are willing to believe; if the rulers oppose, they follow in opposing. This is not faith but group psychology.
Verse 27 shows another, deeper problem:
“However we know where this man comes from, but when the Christ comes, no one will know where he comes from.”
They thought they “knew” Jesus' background, so they concluded He could not be the Christ. Their logic was:
“We know where Jesus is from—Nazareth. But the Christ should be mysteriously sent by God, and no one should know His origin.”
They had a set of imaginings about “what the Messiah should be like,” but these imaginings did not come from Scripture at all; they came from human tradition, human expectation, and human memory.

They took their own notions as truth, and so: the truth was in front of them, yet they could not see it. The Savior was before their eyes, yet they did not recognize Him. Christ stood among them in person, yet they rejected Him because of their notions.
Once a person places his own thinking above God's revelation, he falls from “thinking he knows” to “missing it completely.”
This passage gives us important reminders:

First, some people cannot believe because of confusion and contradiction. They look at people, circumstances, and the direction of the wind, but do not sincerely look at Jesus. Faith not built on Jesus is shaky faith.
Second, some follow power rather than truth. They watch the rulers' attitude more than God's will. Such faith will keep wavering with outside changes.
Third, some reject Jesus because of their own notions. They think they have grasped the truth, yet what they think is right blocks God's true revelation.
Fourth, the greatest blindness is not “not knowing” but “thinking we know.” This makes it harder to surrender, harder to turn, harder to believe.
Fifth, Jesus is right before their eyes, but the truth about the human heart is revealed in how it reacts to Him—the humble see Him, the proud miss Him.
q: With what eyes do you look at Jesus today?
Do you follow human thinking, or are you willing to lay down your own notions and receive the truth He reveals to you Himself?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, remove every blindness from our hearts, so that we no longer limit Your work with our own notions. Let us no longer look at people's opinions, no longer watch the wind, no longer follow the mainstream, but look to You alone. Give us humble hearts, willing to admit that Your thoughts are higher than our thoughts and Your ways higher than our ways. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: Jesus therefore cried out in the temple, teaching and saying, “You both know me, and know where I am from. I have not come of myself, but he who sent me is true, whom you don’t know.
I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me.”
They sought therefore to take him; but no one laid a hand on him, because his hour had not yet come.
But of the multitude, many believed in him. They said, “When the Christ comes, he won’t do more signs than those which this man has done, will he?”
b: This passage unfolds a vivid contrast: the clearer the truth, the more hearts are divided. The brighter the light shines, the stronger people react.
The passage begins:
“Jesus therefore cried out in the temple, teaching and saying, ‘You both know me, and know where I am from…’”

Jesus was not weak or afraid to state His identity openly; He was not discussing it in secret but proclaiming it loudly. He did not fear the threats of the religious leaders; He was faithful to the truth and to His mission.
He said:
“I have not come of myself.”
Once more He declares that His origin is not earthly, that He is not here for Himself, not for fame, position, or applause; everything He does is because the Father sent Him.
His life is completely emptied of self, His actions come entirely from the Father's will, and His words are in complete accord with the Father's heart.
Then He says:
“He who sent me is true, whom you don't know.”
Here Jesus points out their spiritual blind spot: they thought they knew God, thought they were familiar with the law, the temple, and the tradition, but they did not actually know the true God.
They looked at the temple but did not know God's heart; they carried the law but did not understand the Lord of the law; they saw Jesus but could not see the Father.
Religion can make people “think they know God,” but only Jesus can make people truly know God.
Jesus continues:
“I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me.”

He does not know God vaguely but completely; He does not understand God from afar but is wholly one with the Father. He knows the Father's heart, the Father's will, the Father's plan. He is from the Father and also in the Father.
The reason His words carry authority and power is precisely that He has an incomparably intimate relationship with the Father at the root.
Next the passage describes a strong reaction:
“They sought therefore to take him.”

Why? Because His words exposed their true spiritual condition: they thought they belonged to God but did not actually know God. When the light shone into the depths of their hearts, they were unwilling to repent and instead wanted to get rid of the one who lit them up.
Yet:
“No one laid his hand on him, because his hour had not yet come.”

No one can move earlier than God, no plan can outrun God's timing, no attack can break through God's protection. Jesus' life was completely within the Father's time, and no one could send Him to the cross ahead of schedule.
Whoever is in God's hand, no darkness can take his life; only when God's time comes will things be accomplished.
Finally, the passage ends with a beautiful picture:
“But of the multitude, many believed in him.”
Although some hated Him, rejected Him, and opposed Him, there were also those who believed in Him because of His miracles, His words, and His life.
They said:
“When the Christ comes, will he do more signs than those which this man has done?”

This is a sober recognition: if Jesus is not the Christ, who else could be? The signs He did, His teaching, the love He showed, all made clear that He was no ordinary man. Their hearts were illumined, and they were willing to receive the light.
This passage reminds us:
First, Jesus always speaks according to truth, not according to people's emotions or circumstances. He proclaims the Father's will loudly, without compromise.
Second, if people stay at the religious exterior, they will “think they know God” without truly knowing Him. The One who truly knows God is Jesus, and He leads us into true knowledge.
Third, when truth is spoken plainly, people show the real state of their lives. Some oppose, some believe; truth always divides people.
Fourth, even when people attack and try to seize Jesus, they cannot do so ahead of God's time. Those who walk in God's will are safe and secure.
Fifth, true faith begins with seeing what Jesus says and does. Those who seek will see, the humble will hear, and the willing will believe.
q: Is your knowledge of Jesus today still in your head, or has it gone deep into your heart?
Are you willing to let His great light shine on you, so that you come to know the Father's heart more?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, open our hearts completely to You, so that we do not stay at religious surface but truly know You. Help us not to reject the light and not to fear the truth, but to be willing to be illumined, guided, and changed. Let our lives be completely in Your timing, because we know that You are in control of all things. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: The Pharisees heard the multitude murmuring these things concerning him, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to arrest him.
Then Jesus said, “I will be with you a little while longer, then I go to him who sent me.
You will seek me, and won’t find me. You can’t come where I am.”
The Jews therefore said among themselves, “Where will this man go that we won’t find him? Will he go to the Dispersion among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?
What is this word that he said, ‘You will seek me, and won’t find me;’ and ‘Where I am, you can’t come’?”
b: This passage uncovers a profound truth: people reject Jesus because they do not know Him; people may seek Jesus yet never find Him again. The key is not that Jesus hides but that the human heart is closed.
The passage begins:
“The Pharisees heard the multitude murmuring these things concerning him, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to arrest him.”

The reason they wanted to arrest Jesus was not that He had done anything wrong, but that His truth shook their position, system, and control. When the heart is controlled by power, the clearer the truth, the more hostile they become.
The Pharisees' reaction tells us: some people do not fail to know the truth; they are unwilling to have it. They do not lack light; they are unwilling to let the light in.
Jesus saw their hearts and knew the time the Father had arranged, so He declared:
“I will be with you a little while longer, then I go to him who sent me.”
Jesus' life was not taken from Him; He completed His mission in the time the Father had set. He knew His time on earth was short and fixed, that no one could shorten it and no one could lengthen it.

He was not running away from people but moving toward the goal the Father had set. He was saying: “My time with you is limited. You can hear Me, see Me, touch Me, respond to Me—but such moments will not last forever.”
Then He says:
“You will seek me, and won't find me; and where I am, you can't come.”
This sentence is deeply startling:
If a person rejects Jesus in the days of opportunity, there will come a day when, even if he wants to find Him, he cannot.
It is not that Jesus is unwilling to be found, but that people have refused for so long that their hearts have turned to stone.
“You can't come” is not because the distance is too great, but because the heart is too hard, too proud, too unwilling to repent, and so has lost the ability to enter His presence.
Jesus was foretelling that He would return to the Father, but none of those who rejected Him could get there by themselves.
Because the only way to the Father is He Himself. To reject Him is to reject the way itself.
Then the Jews' reaction reveals their blindness:
“Where will this man go that we won't find him? Will he go to the Dispersion among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?”
They explained everything with earthly eyes and guessed with human logic. They thought Jesus was talking about geography, not knowing He was speaking of heavenly truth.

This is the greatest predicament of those who do not know Jesus: they hear His words and do not understand; they see His actions and do not comprehend; He speaks of heavenly things, and people explain them with earthly notions.
Finally, the passage says:
“What is this word that he said?”

They did not understand because they refused to let truth shine into their hearts. Without repentance, they cannot hear. Without surrender, they cannot see. Without willingness to believe, they cannot enter His revelation.
This passage reminds us:
First, some people care not about truth but about maintaining their position. The more such people hear the truth, the more they want to seize Jesus.
Second, Jesus' presence with people is grace, not something to take for granted. He gives everyone time to repent and believe, but that time is not forever.
Third, those who reject Jesus will one day seek Him and not find Him. It is not that Jesus hides, but that the heart can no longer respond.
Fourth, looking at heavenly things with earthly eyes leads to complete error. Heavenly things require humility, surrender, and the illumination of the Holy Spirit.
Fifth, the only ones who can truly reach the Father are those who are willing to receive Jesus. He is the way, the truth, and the life; unless through Him, no one can come to the Father.
q: Are you experiencing Jesus' reminder, call, and invitation today?
Are you willing, while He can still be found, to respond to Him and surrender to Him with all your heart?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, soften our hearts, so that we not only hear Your word but are willing to respond to Your call. Let us not miss the moment You have given us, not harden our hearts or close the door of our hearts. Help us understand that those who can truly reach You are those who humbly receive Jesus and surrender in His grace. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: Now on the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink!
He who believes in me, as the Scripture has said, from within him will flow rivers of living water.”
But he said this about the Spirit, which those believing in him were to receive. For the Holy Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus wasn’t yet glorified.
b: 這三節是整章的高潮，是耶穌在住棚節中的最強宣告。祂在眾人面前揭示一個驚天的真理——祂不是來給人宗教，而是來給人生命；祂不是來給人儀式，而是來給人活水；祂不是來給人道理，而是來給人聖靈。
經文開始說：
「節期的末日，就是最大之日，耶穌站著高聲說……」
住棚節的最後一天，是喜樂最盛大的一天。祭司們會舀水、倒水，象徵求神賜雨，預表盼望神賜下生命的泉源。
就在這個刻意強調「水」的時刻，耶穌站出來，高聲宣告：真正的水、真正的生命、真正的泉源不是儀式、不是水缸、不是宗教傳統，而是祂自己。
這一刻，祂讓整個節期的象徵得以應驗。
祂說：
「人若渴了，可以到我這裡來喝！」
祂不是只對某一群人說，不是對有功德的人，不是對懂律法的人，不是對宗教高層的人，祂是對「任何渴的人」說。
渴的人，才能喝。知道自己缺乏的人，才能領受。承認自己不能的人，才能得著。
祂不是給滿足的人，而是給渴的人；不是給自以為義的人，而是給知道自己不行的人。
而祂給的不是暫時的補給，不是一杯水，而是永恆的活水。
接著祂說：
「信我的人，就如經上所說：從他腹中要流出活水的江河來。」
祂不只是要解我們的渴，祂要把我們變成泉源。
祂不是要我們只作一個接收者，祂要我們成為一個流通者。
活水不是停在裡面，而是流出去。生命不是只為自己，而是湧流給人。聖靈不是只給恩典，而是讓恩典成為生命的河流。
這裡有三個重要的啟示：
第一，「腹中」指最深處，也就是人的靈。神的生命不是停在外表，而是進入最深的內裡。
第二，「活水」不是死水、不是宗教、不是知識，是能改變生命的聖靈。
第三，「江河」不是涓涓細流，不是偶爾滴下，而是持續、澎湃、湧流的生命。
這不是人做出來，而是聖靈湧出來。
第三十九節揭示一切的核心：
「耶穌這話是指著信祂之人要受聖靈說的。」
耶穌不是在講靈修技巧、心靈療癒、宗教感覺，祂是在宣告：真正的生命來自聖靈，真正的泉源是聖靈，真正的滿足是聖靈，真正的能力是聖靈。
沒有聖靈，人只會渴。有了聖靈，人不但得飽足，還能讓別人因我們而得飽足。
經文補上一句：
「那時還沒有賜下聖靈來，因為耶穌尚未得著榮耀。」
耶穌的榮耀是什麼？是十字架、復活、升天。耶穌得榮耀後，祂就把聖靈澆灌下來，讓每一位信祂的人都成為活水的管道。
這段經文提醒我們：
第一，耶穌不是來建立宗教，而是來賜下生命。祂的目標不是讓我們守規條，而是讓我們得著活水。
第二，渴的人才會到耶穌那裡。自以為滿足的人不會來到祂面前。
第三，到祂那裡不是行為，而是關係；不是努力，而是相信；不是表現，而是降服。
第四，真正的生命不是領受一點，而是湧流不止。聖靈不是暫時的感動，而是持續的泉源。
第五，耶穌要我們不只是被填滿，而是湧流出去。祂不是讓我們作一個水缸，而是作一條河。
q: 你今天的生命是乾渴的，還是湧流的？
你是否願意把心完全交給聖靈，讓祂使你成為活水的江河？
pr: 親愛的天父，我們承認我們裡面常常乾渴，世界的水不能讓我們滿足，唯有耶穌的活水才能真正使我們得著生命。今天我們到祢面前，願祢的聖靈充滿我們，使我們不只是得飽足，也成為活水的管道，讓生命從我們裡面湧流出去。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: Many of the multitude therefore, when they heard these words, said, “This is truly the prophet.”
Others said, “This is the Christ.” But some said, “What, does the Christ come out of Galilee?
Hasn’t the Scripture said that the Christ comes of the offspring of David,  and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?”
So a division arose in the multitude because of him.
Some of them would have arrested him, but no one laid hands on him.
b: 這段經文顯示出耶穌的話語與祂的同在如何讓人心立即暴露出來。同一位耶穌、同一段教導、同一個現場，卻出現完全不同的反應——有人相信、有人誤解、有人拒絕、有人敵對。真理不會讓所有人一致，它會讓所有人表明立場。
經文開始說：
「許多人聽見這話，就說：這真是那先知。」
「那先知」指的是申命記18章摩西所預言的先知，即將來要像摩西的彌賽亞性質的領袖。這些人看到耶穌的權柄、祂的生命、祂滿有恩典與真理的教導，心裡的確認知到祂不像普通拉比，祂是神所應許要來的人。
但他們還不夠明白，只承認祂是「先知」，不是「基督」。他們的眼光已經開始被光照，但還沒有完全看清。
接著另一群人更進一步：
「也有人說：這是基督。」
這些人看見耶穌的神蹟、祂的愛、祂的權柄、祂的生命，他們心中確信：這不是普通人，不是先知，而是神差來的基督。
真信心在人群中常常是微小的、不是主流的，但總是存在。耶穌的光使那些謙卑尋求神的人得以看見真理。
然而，總會有人反對。
41、42節顯示第三種反應：
「但也有人說：基督豈是從加利利出來的嗎？」「經上豈不是說：基督是大衛的後裔，從伯利恆出來的嗎？」
這些人的反對不是基於真理，而是基於「以為知道」的錯誤資訊。
他們以為耶穌是加利利人，卻不知道祂其實是在伯利恆出生。他們以為祂不是大衛後裔，卻不知道祂正是大衛的子孫。
他們的反對不是因為真理，而是因為無知、偏見、聽說、錯誤的印象。
這對我們是一個深刻提醒：人心最容易因為不完整的資訊而拒絕神最完整的啟示。對耶穌的錯誤認知，比不認識祂更致命。
他們的錯誤觀念拔起了一道牆，讓他們看不見真正的基督。
接著經文說：
「於是眾人因著耶穌起了分爭。」
這樣的結局不是意外，而是必然。
真理一出現，人群一定會被分開。光越亮，人心越顯露。耶穌不會讓人保持中立，祂要人表明態度，而不是模糊地跟著群體走。
祂來到世上，不是要製造混亂，而是要揭露真實。
而最後一節顯示第四種反應：
「其中有人要捉拿祂，只是無人下手。」
他們對耶穌的光不是感恩，而是恨惡。他們不但不相信，還想除掉祂。但沒有人下手——因為：
一、耶穌的時候還沒有到；
二、神的手攔阻；
三、耶穌的生命有天父的保護；
四、人的惡意不能勝過神的旨意。
這段經文提醒我們：
第一，聽到真理的人，不會都做同樣反應。有的人會被吸引，有的人會被光照，有的人會被冒犯，有的人會敵對。
第二，自以為知道的人最容易錯過基督。那些以為耶穌從加利利來的人，他們的觀念反而阻擋了他們認識救主。
第三，人若只憑表面資訊，就無法認識耶穌。必須謙卑尋求，才能看見真理。
第四，耶穌的到來，讓人的真實屬靈狀態完全暴露。祂是分辨人心的光。
第五，沒有任何攻擊能早於神的時間臨到耶穌。同樣，凡在神旨意裡的人，也是穩妥的。
q: 你是用自己的觀念認識耶穌，還是真正讓祂向你啟示祂自己？
今天，你願意求主光照你的眼睛，使你看見祂真的是基督嗎？
pr: 親愛的天父，求祢使我們的眼睛被祢真光照亮，使我們不再憑印象、不再依賴人的傳說，而是真正按著聖經與聖靈的光認識耶穌。求祢保守我們的心，使我們不落在錯誤的觀念裡，而是單單接受祢的啟示。願我們永遠站在真理的這一邊，願意跟隨基督到底。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: The officers therefore came to the chief priests and Pharisees, and they said to them, “Why didn’t you bring him?”
The officers answered, “No man ever spoke like this man!”
The Pharisees therefore answered them, “You aren’t also led astray, are you?
Have any of the rulers believed in him, or of the Pharisees?
But this multitude that doesn’t know the law is cursed.”
b: 這段經文是一場極強烈的對比：一邊是被耶穌話語震撼的差役，另一邊是被驕傲與權勢綑綁的宗教領袖。同樣都聽見耶穌說話，但有人心被打開，有人心更加剛硬。
經文開始：
「差役回到祭司長和法利賽人那裡。」
這些差役原本被派去做一件事──捉拿耶穌。他們帶著命令而去，卻空手而回。
宗教領袖很不滿，立刻質問：
「你們為什麼沒有帶祂來呢？」
在他們眼中，耶穌只是「目標」、是「問題」、是「威脅」，他們不關心真理，只關心控制。他們期待的是服從命令，而不是聽見真理。
但差役的回答非常震撼：
「從來沒有像祂這樣說話的！」
這不是一個神學分析，不是深奧理論，而是一群普通人最直接的感受：
耶穌的話不一樣。
祂的話不是知識，而是生命；不是宗教語言，而是帶著權柄與光；不是空洞教條，而是能刺入人心深處。
差役原本是來抓耶穌，卻被耶穌的話抓住。
他們原本是執行命令的人，卻在聽見真理後停下腳步。
這讓我們看見：真正帶著聖靈能力的話語，會讓人無法忽略。
耶穌不像一般拉比引述別人的話，祂直接說：「我實實在在告訴你們……」祂的話帶著天上的權柄，因為祂自己就是真理。
然而，法利賽人的反應卻暴露了他們真正的問題。
他們說：
「你們也受了迷惑嗎？」
他們沒有思考差役為何被震撼，沒有問耶穌到底說了什麼，沒有尋求真理，他們第一個反應是──否定。
驕傲的人不會先聽真理，而會先保護自己的立場。
接著他們說：
「官長或法利賽人，豈有信祂的呢？」
這句話揭露出他們信仰最深的根基──不是神，而是權威與群體認同。
他們的意思是：
「我們這些懂律法的人都不信，所以祂一定不對。」
他們把「人的地位」當成真理的標準。但屬靈真理從來不是多數決，也不是權勢決定。神的真理常常是少數人看見的。
很多時候，真正攔阻人信主的，不是沒有證據，而是「怕跟主流不一樣」。
最後，第49節是整段最令人心寒的一句：
「但這些不明白律法的百姓，是被咒詛的！」
這是宗教驕傲最赤裸的表現。
他們看不起百姓，覺得自己屬靈、別人低等；覺得自己懂律法、別人無知；覺得自己代表神、別人不配。
但最諷刺的是：真正離神最遠的，往往是最自以為懂神的人。
他們熟悉聖經，卻不認識基督；他們研究律法，卻拒絕生命；他們談論神，卻敵擋神的兒子。
這段經文提醒我們：
第一，耶穌的話與世上一切話語不同。祂的話帶著生命、權柄與聖靈的能力。
第二，真理能抓住最普通的人。差役沒有神學背景，卻比宗教領袖更接近真理。
第三，驕傲的人很難接受真理。因為他們首先保護的不是神，而是自己的位置。
第四，不要把人的地位當成真理的標準。真正的真理來自神，不來自群體壓力。
第五，宗教驕傲會讓人看不起別人，也看不見自己。真正屬神的人越認識神，越謙卑。
q: 當耶穌的話光照你時，你是像差役一樣被觸動，還是像法利賽人一樣先保護自己的立場？
你願意今天放下驕傲，單純讓主的話抓住你的心嗎？
pr: 親愛的天父，求祢讓我們的心像那些差役一樣，願意被祢的話觸摸，而不是像法利賽人一樣被驕傲蒙蔽。求祢除去我們裡面自以為義、自以為懂的心，使我們單純、謙卑地來到耶穌面前。願祢的話天天抓住我們，使我們的生命被真理更新。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: Nicodemus (he who came to him by night, being one of them) said to them,
“Does our law judge a man, unless it first hears from him personally and knows what he does?”
They answered him, “Are you also from Galilee? Search, and see that no prophet has arisen out of Galilee.”
Everyone went to his own house,
b: 這段經文雖然簡短，卻是一幅極深刻的人心圖畫。在一片敵對、控告與情緒中，尼哥底母微弱卻勇敢地站出來，為耶穌說了一句公道話。這段經文讓我們看見：在黑暗最深的時候，仍然有人願意向真理靠近；但人若被驕傲掌控，就連律法本身也會被利用來拒絕真理。
經文一開始提到：
「內中有尼哥底母，就是從前去見耶穌的。」
這提醒我們約翰福音第三章的故事。當時尼哥底母是在夜裡偷偷去見耶穌的人。他有渴慕，但不敢公開；他有問題，但還沒有完全相信；他心裡被耶穌吸引，卻仍活在人的眼光與宗教壓力裡。
如今，在第七章裡，他開始有了改變。
他沒有立刻公開宣告：「耶穌是基督。」但他願意站出來說一句公義的話。對當時的環境而言，這已經是很大的跨越。
他說：
「不先聽本人的口供，不知道他所做的事，難道我們的律法還定他的罪嗎？」
尼哥底母沒有直接替耶穌辯護，他只是回到最基本的公平：
「難道不應該先聽祂說嗎？」
這句話看似簡單，其實是在光照法利賽人的虛假。
他們天天高舉律法，卻連律法最基本的公義都不願遵守。他們口裡談公平，心裡卻早已定了耶穌的罪。
這是宗教驕傲最可怕的地方：人會利用真理來抵擋真理，利用律法來敵擋神。
尼哥底母提醒他們：真正的律法是公平的，真正的真理是不預設立場的。
然而，法利賽人的反應非常真實：
「你也是出於加利利嗎？」
他們沒有回答問題，而是攻擊人。因為當人沒有真理可以站立時，就會開始人身攻擊。
他們的意思是：
「你是不是也被耶穌影響了？你是不是站在祂那邊？你是不是也變成那群沒知識的人？」
驕傲的人最怕別人不同意自己，所以他們會用羞辱、標籤、壓力來控制群體。
接著他們又說：
「你去查考，就知道加利利沒有出過先知。」
這句話本身就是錯的。約拿就是加利利附近的人，但他們因著情緒與偏見，已經不在乎真理。
這讓我們看見：
當人拒絕真光時，即使熟讀聖經，也會被自己的偏見蒙蔽。
最後，第53節說：
「於是各人都回家去了。」
這句話很安靜，卻很沉重。
耶穌沒有被接納，真理沒有被認真對待，人們帶著自己的偏見與立場散去。
各人回家，但問題沒有解決；真理仍然站在他們面前，只是他們不願降服。
這節也像是在提醒我們：
聚會可以結束，討論可以散去，但人是否真正回應耶穌，才是最重要的事。
這段經文提醒我們：
第一，真理常常是在壓力中被顯明。尼哥底母雖然還不完全，但他開始願意站向光。
第二，真正屬神的人會尊重公平與真理。不預設立場、不隨眾定罪。
第三，驕傲的人不會回答真理，而會攻擊人。因為他們真正保護的是自己的地位。
第四，熟悉聖經不等於認識神。若沒有謙卑，再多知識也可能變成蒙蔽。
第五，每個人最後都要決定：是回家繼續過自己的生活，還是真正回應站在面前的耶穌。
q: 當真理與群體壓力衝突時，你會選擇站在哪一邊？
你願意像尼哥底母一樣，即使不完全，也開始勇敢靠近光嗎？
pr: 親愛的天父，求祢使我們像尼哥底母一樣，即使還軟弱，也願意向真理靠近。除去我們裡面的偏見、驕傲與先入為主，使我們不只是研究真理，而是真正降服於真理。求祢讓我們不只是聽見耶穌，而是真正回應祂。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: but Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
Now very early in the morning, he came again into the temple, and all the people came to him. He sat down and taught them.
The scribes and the Pharisees brought a woman taken in adultery. Having set her in the middle,
they told him, “Teacher, we found this woman in adultery, in the very act.
Now in our law, Moses commanded us to stone such women. What then do you say about her?”
They said this testing him, that they might have something to accuse him of. But Jesus stooped down and wrote on the ground with his finger.
b: 這段經文是聖經中極深刻的一幕。一邊是人的定罪、羞辱與陷害；另一邊是耶穌的安靜、智慧與憐憫。而整個故事最核心的焦點，不只是那婦人的罪，而是──人如何利用別人的罪，來掩蓋自己的罪。
經文一開始說：
「各人都回家去了；耶穌卻往橄欖山去。」
眾人散去，回到自己的生活；耶穌卻選擇往橄欖山去。橄欖山是祂常常禱告、與父交通的地方。這讓我們看見：耶穌所有的能力、智慧與愛，不是從人來的，而是從與父親密的關係而來。
第二天清早，祂又回到殿裡教訓人。祂並沒有因人的敵意停止服事，反而持續忠心地把真理帶給人。
就在這時，一群文士和法利賽人帶來一個婦人。
經文特別說：
「叫她站在當中。」
這不只是法律問題，更是一場公開羞辱。
她被推到人群中央，成為眾人的焦點、控告的對象、宗教表演的工具。
更值得注意的是：經文只提到婦人，卻沒有提那個男人。按照律法，犯淫亂的男女都應被處理。但他們只抓女人。這顯示他們真正目的不是公義，而是利用。
接著他們對耶穌說：
「摩西在律法上吩咐我們把這樣的婦人用石頭打死。你說該把她怎麼樣呢？」
這是一個陷阱。
如果耶穌說「赦免她」，他們就能控告祂違反摩西律法；如果耶穌說「打死她」，祂就失去祂憐憫與恩典的形象。
他們不是在尋求真理，而是在設局陷害。他們不在乎婦人的生命，也不在乎神的心意，他們只想利用人的失敗來攻擊耶穌。
這就是宗教最可怕的黑暗：利用真理來傷害人，利用律法來高舉自己，利用別人的罪來遮蓋自己的驕傲。
然而，第六節出現一個極安靜、卻極有力量的畫面：
「耶穌卻彎著腰，用指頭在地上畫字。」
祂沒有立刻回答，沒有情緒反應，沒有被人帶進控告與混亂。
祂安靜下來。
這份安靜不是軟弱，而是屬天的權柄。祂沒有被人的陷阱拉著走，因為祂活在父的平安裡。
很多時候，人用情緒推動事情，但耶穌用安靜勝過混亂。人想立刻定罪，耶穌卻先停下來。
祂知道真正需要被處理的，不只是婦人的罪，更是那些拿石頭之人的心。
這段經文提醒我們：
第一，很多人對罪有興趣，卻對人沒有憐憫。法利賽人看重律法，卻失去愛。
第二，人很容易利用別人的失敗來抬高自己。這就是驕傲與有己的生命。
第三，真正屬神的人，不會急著定罪，而會先來到父面前。耶穌的安靜來自祂與父的連結。
第四，宗教若失去愛，就會變成傷害人的工具。真理若沒有恩典，就會變成石頭。
第五，耶穌看見的不只是人的行為，而是人的內心。祂知道誰真正犯罪，也知道誰正在假裝公義。
q: 你是否曾經像法利賽人一樣，用別人的問題來顯出自己的對？
今天，你願不願意放下手中的石頭，學習耶穌的憐憫與安靜？
pr: 親愛的天父，求祢保守我們的心，不讓我們成為只會定罪別人的人。求祢讓我們像耶穌一樣，有從祢而來的安靜、智慧與憐憫。當我們看見別人的軟弱時，不是高舉石頭，而是高舉恩典；不是驕傲控告，而是帶著愛與真理。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: But when they continued asking him, he looked up and said to them, “He who is without sin among you, let him throw the first stone at her.”
Again he stooped down and wrote on the ground with his finger.
They, when they heard it, being convicted by their conscience, went out one by one, beginning from the oldest, even to the last. Jesus was left alone with the woman where she was, in the middle.
Jesus, standing up, saw her and said, “Woman, where are your accusers? Did no one condemn you?”
She said, “No one, Lord.” Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way. From now on, sin no more.”
b: 這段經文是福音最美的畫面之一。耶穌既沒有否認罪，也沒有縱容罪；祂既有真理，也有恩典；祂既讓人看見自己的黑暗，也給人重新開始的盼望。
整段經文的中心不是婦人的罪，而是──耶穌如何面對罪人。
經文開始說：
「他們還是不住地問祂。」
法利賽人不肯停下，因為他們想逼耶穌表態。他們不是尋求公義，而是渴望定罪。他們不想救人，只想贏。
於是耶穌終於直起腰來，說出一句震撼千古的話：
「你們中間誰是沒有罪的，誰就可以先拿石頭打她。」
耶穌沒有說婦人沒罪。祂承認罪是真實的。但祂把焦點從「別人的罪」轉向「自己的罪」。
法利賽人以為自己是審判者，耶穌卻讓他們發現：其實他們也是罪人。
這句話像一道光照進每個人的良心。
原本大家只看婦人的罪，現在卻開始看見自己的罪。原本大家手裡拿著石頭，現在卻開始發現自己的心也是石頭。
接著經文說：
「耶穌又彎著腰，用指頭在地上畫字。」
祂說完後沒有追擊、沒有羞辱、沒有乘勝追打。祂再次安靜下來。
真正有權柄的人，不需要靠情緒壓制人。真正從神來的真理，不是讓人絕望，而是讓人醒悟。
然後，第九節是一幅極震撼的畫面：
「從老到少，一個一個地都出去了。」
為什麼從老到少？因為年紀越大的人，越知道自己裡面的罪與黑暗。他們原本以為自己站在光裡，現在才發現自己也需要恩典。
石頭沒有丟出去，因為真光已經照進每個人的良心。
最後，現場只剩兩個人：
「只剩下耶穌一人，還有那婦人仍然站在當中。」
一個是完全聖潔、真正有資格定罪的人；一個是滿身羞愧、真正有罪的人。
而這，就是福音。
真正無罪的主，站在真正有罪的人面前。
接著耶穌問：
「沒有人定你的罪嗎？」
婦人說：
「主啊，沒有。」
於是耶穌說出福音最溫柔的一句話：
「我也不定你的罪。」
這不是因為她沒罪，而是因為耶穌將來要替她承擔罪。祂不是忽略罪，祂是預備自己上十字架。
祂不是說罪沒關係，而是說：「我願意替你承擔。」
但耶穌沒有停在恩典，祂接著說：
「去吧！從此不要再犯罪了。」
真正的恩典不是縱容，真正的愛不是放任。耶穌赦免人，是為了讓人得自由；耶穌接納人，是為了讓人改變。
祂不是只把婦人從石頭下救出來，祂更要把她從罪裡救出來。
這段經文提醒我們：
第一，人很容易看見別人的罪，卻看不見自己的罪。只有真光照進來，我們才會真正認識自己。
第二，真正有資格定罪的耶穌，卻選擇憐憫。而最沒有資格定罪的人，往往最喜歡定罪別人。
第三，恩典不是否認罪，而是承擔罪。耶穌不是說罪不重要，而是祂願意為罪付代價。
第四，真正的赦免會帶來生命的改變。「不要再犯罪了」不是要求，而是新的開始。
第五，福音不是「你沒罪」，而是「你有罪，但耶穌愛你，並願意救你」。這才是真正的恩典。
q: 你手裡是否也曾拿著石頭，準備定別人的罪？
今天，你願不願意放下石頭，也讓耶穌的恩典重新恢復你？
pr: 親愛的天父，謝謝祢沒有按我們的罪待我們，而是在耶穌裡向我們施恩。求祢除去我們裡面驕傲定罪人的心，也求祢讓我們真正看見自己的需要。謝謝耶穌不定我們的罪，並給我們重新開始的機會。求祢幫助我們離開罪，活出新的生命。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: Again, therefore, Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. He who follows me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”
b: 這節經文雖然只有短短一句，卻是整本約翰福音最重要的宣告之一。耶穌不只是帶來光，祂自己就是光。祂不是教人怎麼找到光，祂就是人生命唯一真正的光源。
而這句話出現在那位行淫婦人得赦免之後，更顯得極其深刻。剛剛耶穌讓人看見：人的黑暗、宗教的黑暗、驕傲的黑暗、罪的黑暗。接著，祂立刻宣告：
「我是世界的光。」
意思是：真正能解決黑暗的，不是律法；不是人的努力；不是宗教制度；不是人的道德；而是耶穌自己。
祂不是照亮一部分，祂是世界的光。不分猶太人、外邦人；不分貧窮、富有；不分過去多黑暗；只要願意來到祂面前，就能得著光。
「光」在聖經裡有很深的含義：
光代表真理。光代表生命。光代表聖潔。光代表神的同在。光代表方向。光代表盼望。
沒有光，人就活在混亂裡；沒有光，人就分不清方向；沒有光，人會把黑暗當正常；沒有光，人甚至不知道自己已經迷路。
今天很多人的問題，不只是做錯事，而是根本活在黑暗裡，卻不知道。人以為自己看得見，其實靈裡是瞎的；人以為自己自由，其實被罪綑綁；人以為自己很清楚，其實方向完全錯了。
所以耶穌不是來「增加一點亮光」，祂是來徹底改變人的生命狀態。
接著祂說：
「跟從我的，就不在黑暗裡走。」
注意，祂不是說：
「知道我的、研究我的、討論我的、欣賞我的。」
而是：
「跟從我的。」
光不是用來欣賞的，是用來跟隨的。
真正的信仰不是停留在知識，而是生命方向的改變。跟從耶穌，代表：
不再跟從自己；不再跟從世界；不再跟從肉體；不再跟從黑暗。
而是讓耶穌決定方向。
很多人想要光，卻不想跟從；想得平安，卻不願降服；想得祝福，卻仍然自己作王。
但耶穌說：真正離開黑暗的方法，不只是「知道光」，而是「跟從光」。
接著祂應許：
「必要得著生命的光。」
不是短暫的亮光，而是「生命的光」。
意思是：這光會進入你的生命裡面。不只是照亮外面，而是改變裡面。
祂會：
照亮你的思想；更新你的價值觀；改變你的眼光；醫治你的黑暗；帶領你走正路；使你從罪與死亡中出來。
世界的光只能照外面，耶穌的光能照進人的靈魂。
而且祂不是讓你偶爾亮一下，祂是讓你得著一個新的生命。
這段經文提醒我們：
第一，耶穌不是帶來光，祂自己就是光。離開祂，生命永遠在黑暗裡。
第二，人最大的問題不是外面的困難，而是裡面的黑暗。只有耶穌能真正照亮人心。
第三，真正的信仰不是欣賞耶穌，而是跟從耶穌。跟從代表放下自己的道路。
第四，耶穌的光不只是外在幫助，而是生命更新。祂要把生命的光放進我們裡面。
第五，黑暗不可怕，拒絕光才可怕。只要願意來到耶穌面前，再深的黑暗都能被照亮。
q: 你生命裡現在有哪些黑暗仍然沒有讓耶穌照進去？
你願意不只是「知道」耶穌，而是真正「跟從」祂嗎？
pr: 親愛的天父，謝謝祢把耶穌賜給我們，成為世界的光。求祢照亮我們生命中一切黑暗的地方，讓我們不再活在自己的裡面，而是真正跟從耶穌。求祢把生命的光放在我們裡面，使我們不再迷失，而是活在祢的真理、平安與生命中。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: The Pharisees therefore said to him, “You testify about yourself. Your testimony is not valid.”
Jesus answered them, “Even if I testify about myself, my testimony is true, for I know where I came from, and where I am going; but you don’t know where I came from, or where I am going.
You judge according to the flesh. I judge no one.
Even if I do judge, my judgment is true, for I am not alone, but I am with the Father who sent me.
It’s also written in your law that the testimony of two people is valid.
I am one who testifies about myself, and the Father who sent me testifies about me.”
b: 這段經文是一場屬天眼光與屬地眼光的衝突。法利賽人看見耶穌，卻不認識祂；耶穌知道自己是誰，也知道自己從哪裡來、往哪裡去。真正的差別，不在外表，而在生命是否活在父的光中。
經文開始：
「法利賽人對祂說：你是為自己作見證，你的見證不真。」
按照猶太律法，一個人的見證需要兩三個人證明才成立。法利賽人抓住這點來攻擊耶穌：
「你一直講自己是光、是從神來的、是基督，這只是你自己說的，不算數。」
但其實，他們不是在追求真理，而是在拒絕真理。因為耶穌早已用祂的神蹟、祂的教導、祂的生命、施洗約翰的見證、聖經的預言來證明自己。
問題從來不是「證據不夠」，而是「人心不願相信」。
接著耶穌回答：
「我雖然為自己作見證，我的見證還是真的；因我知道我從哪裡來，往哪裡去。」
這句話非常重要。
耶穌的確據不是建立在人怎麼看祂，而是建立在祂與父的關係。
祂知道：
祂從父而來；祂為父而活；祂要回到父那裡去。
因此祂不需要靠人的認同來證明自己。
很多人的生命之所以不穩，是因為不知道自己從哪裡來、為何而活、要往哪裡去。所以拼命尋求人肯定、尋求地位、尋求價值感。
但耶穌完全不一樣。祂裡面沒有不安，因為祂知道自己是誰。
接著祂對法利賽人說：
「你們卻不知道我從哪裡來，往哪裡去。」
他們最大的問題不是知識不夠，而是屬靈的瞎眼。
他們看得見耶穌的外表，卻看不見祂的源頭。他們知道祂肉身的背景，卻不知道祂是從父來的。
這就是屬肉體的人：只能看外面，無法看見屬靈的真相。
於是耶穌接著說：
「你們是以外貌判斷人。」
這正是法利賽人的核心問題。
他們看：
背景、學歷、地位、傳統、規條、外在。他們用人的標準衡量神。
他們以為自己在判斷耶穌，其實真正被顯明的是他們自己的黑暗。
而耶穌說：
「我卻不判斷人。」
意思不是祂沒有分辨，而是祂不是像人一樣按外貌、按偏見、按肉體定罪。
祂若判斷，祂的判斷是真實的，因為祂不是憑自己，而是與父完全合一。
接著祂說：
「不是我獨自在這裡，還有差我來的父與我同在。」
這是耶穌力量的根源。
祂從不孤單。祂每一句話、每一個決定、每一步道路，都與父同行。
人最大的安全感，不是有人支持自己，而是知道父與自己同在。
最後耶穌說：
「我為自己作見證，還有差我來的父也是為我作見證。」
父怎麼為祂作見證？
透過：
聖經預言；施洗約翰；神蹟奇事；聖靈能力；父從天上的聲音；耶穌的生命本身。
耶穌不是孤單的見證者，整個天都在為祂作見證。
這段經文提醒我們：
第一，人若不願相信，再多證據也沒用。問題不是缺少光，而是拒絕光。
第二，真正穩定的生命，來自知道自己從哪裡來、往哪裡去。耶穌的確據來自祂與父的關係。
第三，屬肉體的人只按外貌判斷。但神看內心，看生命，看真理。
第四，耶穌不憑自己行事，祂始終與父同在。這也是祂能力與平安的來源。
第五，我們若活在父的同在裡，就不需要靠世界來證明自己。因為真正的價值，來自神的認定。
q: 你現在的價值感，是建立在人怎麼看你，還是建立在天父怎麼看你？
你是否願意像耶穌一樣，不再憑外貌判斷，而是活在父的眼光裡？
pr: 親愛的天父，求祢讓我們不再活在人的眼光與肯定裡，而是像耶穌一樣，知道自己從祢而來，也要回到祢那裡去。求祢除去我們按外貌判斷人的心，使我們學會用祢的眼光看人、看事、看自己。也求祢讓我們天天活在祢的同在中，不再孤單、不再不安。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: They said therefore to him, “Where is your Father?” Jesus answered, “You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, you would know my Father also.”
Jesus spoke these words in the treasury, as he taught in the temple. Yet no one arrested him, because his hour had not yet come.
b: 這段經文雖然簡短，卻揭開一個極深的真理：人若不認識耶穌，就不可能真正認識父；而真正認識耶穌的人，就會進入與父的關係。
法利賽人聽見耶穌一直提到「父」，於是問祂：
「你的父在哪裡？」
他們以為耶穌是在講地上的父親，或是在要求祂提出「見證人」。但其實，耶穌所說的是天父。
這再次顯示一件事：屬肉體的人永遠只能理解地上的層面，無法進入屬靈的真理。
他們與耶穌面對面，卻完全不知道祂在講什麼。這是最深的屬靈瞎眼。
於是耶穌回答：
「你們不認識我，也不認識我的父。」
這句話直接揭露了法利賽人的真實狀態。
他們自認最懂神；熟讀律法；天天在聖殿；研究聖經；帶領百姓；卻被耶穌直接指出：
「你們根本不認識父。」
這是何等震撼！
原來：
懂宗教，不等於認識神；懂聖經知識，不等於認識父；有屬靈外表，不等於與神有關係。
真正認識父的唯一道路，就是耶穌。
因此祂接著說：
「若是認識我，也就認識我的父。」
耶穌不是只介紹父，祂是父的顯明。祂不是帶來一部分神的資訊，祂是神榮耀所發的光輝。
看見耶穌的愛，就是看見父的愛；看見耶穌的憐憫，就是看見父的憐憫；看見耶穌的真理，就是看見父的真理。
所以，離開耶穌，人永遠只能停留在宗教裡，無法真正進入與父的關係。
這也是今天很多人的問題：知道很多關於神的事，卻不認識神的心。會講神學，卻不懂父的愛。會服事，卻不親近主。
因為真正的生命，不是知識累積，而是與耶穌連結。
接著第20節說：
「這些話是耶穌在殿裡的庫房、教訓人時所說的。」
庫房是在聖殿中人很多的地方，代表耶穌是在公開場合說這些話。祂不是私下說，不是偷偷講，而是光明正大地宣告真理。
祂不怕人的敵意，因為祂完全活在父的旨意裡。
最後一句很重要：
「也沒有人拿祂，因為祂的時候還沒有到。」
這句話在約翰福音不斷重複。
人想抓祂，卻抓不到；人想殺祂，卻不能動手。
因為耶穌不是活在人手裡，而是活在父的時間裡。
真正掌管祂生命的，不是敵人，而是天父。
這對我們是一個很大的安慰：
若我們活在神的旨意中，人生不在環境手裡，不在人的惡意手裡，不在撒但手裡，而是在父的手裡。
沒有任何事情能早於神的允許臨到我們。
這段經文提醒我們：
第一，不認識耶穌的人，不可能真正認識父。耶穌是唯一通往父的道路。
第二，宗教知識不等於生命關係。真正認識神，是透過與耶穌連結。
第三，耶穌是父最完全的顯明。看見祂，就是看見父的心。
第四，耶穌不活在人的控制裡，而是活在父的時間裡。這是祂真正的平安與權柄來源。
第五，真正屬神的人，也能在混亂世界中活出安穩。因為知道父掌管一切。
q: 你對神的認識，是停留在知識，還是真正與耶穌建立關係？
今天，你願不願意更深認識耶穌，好讓你真正認識天父？
pr: 親愛的天父，謝謝祢藉著耶穌向我們顯明祢自己。求祢讓我們不只是停留在宗教知識裡，而是真正認識祢的心。幫助我們天天更深與耶穌連結，使我們越來越像祂。也求祢讓我們學會安息在祢的主權中，相信我們的人生在祢手裡。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。

v: Jesus said therefore again to them, “I am going away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sins. Where I go, you can’t come.”
The Jews therefore said, “Will he kill himself, because he says, ‘Where I am going, you can’t come’?”
He said to them, “You are from beneath. I am from above. You are of this world. I am not of this world.
I said therefore to you that you will die in your sins; for unless you believe that I am he, you will die in your sins.”
b: 這段經文是耶穌極嚴肅的一段警告。祂不只是指出人的問題，更指出人若拒絕祂，最終的結局。
而整段經文的核心只有一句話：
「你們若不信我是基督，必要死在罪中。」
這不是威脅，而是真相。
耶穌首先說：
「我要去了，你們要找我。」
祂再次預告自己將要離開世界、回到父那裡。但祂說：將來有一天，人會想找祂，卻找不到。
這是何等沉重的話。
今天人可以忽略耶穌、推開耶穌、拖延回應耶穌，但有一天，人會發現：真正需要祂時，自己卻仍然拒絕過祂。
接著祂說：
「你們要死在罪中。」
這句話極其嚴肅。
人最大的問題不是環境，不是痛苦，不是缺乏，不是失敗，而是──罪。
罪使人與神隔絕；罪使人活在黑暗；罪使人無法進入永生；罪讓人即使活著，裡面卻是死的。
而最可怕的是：人若拒絕耶穌，就沒有罪得赦免的道路。
「死在罪中」不只是肉體死亡，而是永遠與神隔絕。
然而，猶太人的反應再次顯示他們屬靈的瞎眼。
他們說：
「難道祂要自盡嗎？」
耶穌講屬天的事，他們卻只用地上的思想理解。
這正是屬世界之人的特徵：只能理解地上的事，無法明白屬靈的事。
於是耶穌直接指出根本差別：
「你們是從下頭來的，我是從上頭來的；你們是屬這世界的，我不是屬這世界的。」
這不是在講地理，而是在講生命源頭。
「從下頭來」代表：屬肉體、屬世界、屬罪、屬黑暗、屬自己。
「從上頭來」代表：屬神、屬真理、屬聖靈、屬天國。
耶穌在說：你們之所以聽不懂我，不是因為我講得不清楚，而是因為你們的生命仍屬這世界。
世界的人用世界的邏輯活；屬神的人用神的真理活。
這也是為什麼人若沒有重生，就無法真正明白神。
最後，耶穌再次重複：
「你們若不信我是基督，必要死在罪中。」
注意，祂重複了兩次「死在罪中」。
因為這是人最根本的問題。
不是宗教不夠，不是修養不夠，不是努力不夠，而是人需要救恩。
而救恩的關鍵，不是行為，而是信。
信什麼？
信「耶穌是基督」。也就是：
祂是神的兒子；祂是救主；祂是唯一道路；祂能赦罪；祂能賜生命；祂能使人從死亡進入永生。
拒絕祂的人，不是沒有宗教，而是沒有生命。
這段經文提醒我們：
第一，人最大的問題不是環境，而是罪。罪使人與神隔絕，也使人活在死亡裡。
第二，耶穌是唯一能解決罪的人。離開祂，人無法真正得生命。
第三，屬世界的人無法明白屬天的真理。唯有重生的人，才能進入神的國。
第四，不信耶穌，不只是少一個宗教選擇，而是仍然死在罪中。
第五，真正的救恩關鍵在於：你是否相信耶穌是基督。
q: 你是否真正相信耶穌不只是老師，而是基督、是救主？
你現在活著的方式，更像屬世界的人，還是屬天國的人？
pr: 親愛的天父，謝謝祢差遣耶穌來拯救我們脫離罪與死亡。求祢開我們的眼睛，使我們不再活在世界的黑暗裡，而是真正相信耶穌是基督，是救主，是生命的主。求祢使我們從罪中得釋放，從死亡進入永生，並活出屬天的生命。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
